olivia_sales: Kicking off the Nebula Health POC handoff thread — they want a perf run focused on 200 RPS sustained for 30m and p99 < 400ms. Need final load plan, cost estimate, and any enterprise blockers (security / VPC).

leo_perf: Thanks — copying proposed test matrix below. Will run on Dedicated staging pool first, then repeat on Hosted with model-quant variants.

leo_perf: TEST MATRIX (short):
- steady: 200 RPS for 30m (90s warmup)
- spike: 800 RPS for 60s every 10m
- burst soak: 400 RPS sustained 10m for concurrency tail checks

leo_perf: we'll exercise seq_len 512 and 1024, batch sizes 1/4/8, and both float16 and q4_0 quant.

aj_patton: How are you generating traffic? k6 or JMeter? Also which endpoint — chat vs completion?

leo_perf: k6 with a small wrapper to preserve token distribution. Hitting /v1/chat/completions with streaming disabled for consistent latency measurement. Example command:
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m nebula_chat_load.js
```

samir_eng: For Dedicated runs I suggest pinning to a single model shard to avoid cross-node variance. I'll create a pool with 4xA10g-equivalent GPUs for the window.

olivia_sales: Security asked about data isolation and audit logs. Nebula Health will require SOC2 attestation and per-request audit logging for the POC. Any blockers?

maya_security: We can provide SOC2 summary and an audit-log export for the POC. However Nebula asked for VPC peering and HSM-backed KMS for keys — that needs a Private deployment evaluation, which adds ~2 weeks and a different pricing tier.

leo_perf: Noted. For initial perf numbers we can run synthetic tests that don't use customer data; that avoids KMS/HSM gating for initial validation. If they insist on production-like keys, we need Private.

olivia_sales: Customer also asked for an estimate of per-1M-request cost at 200 RPS sustained vs bursty pattern. Can you give a quick back-of-envelope?

leo_perf: Rough math: serving runtime + GPU utilization -> on Dedicated with 4xA10g pool and our batching profile expect ~0.8 tokens/sec/GPU. For typical chat sessions (avg 150 tokens generated) cost ~= $0.18/request at current committed pricing. For 1M requests that's ~$180k. If we enable aggressive KV prefix caching and q4_0 we'll drop to ~0.11/request (~$110k). Those are approximate — I'll produce a precise table after the first run.

aj_patton: Can we include automated trace hooks so we can correlate request id -> token breakdown? Sales wants per-route cost reporting visible to customer during POC.

leo_perf: Yep — we'll enable token-level tracing and a temporary dashboard in Console. I can add a route filter to show tail latency percentiles.

devops-bot: Scheduled run created: Dedicated-staging pool 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC (3h window).

samir_eng: I'll provision the pool and share SSH/test creds. Also will seed model cache before the window to avoid cold-start spikes.

olivia_sales: Great. Next steps / owners:
- leo_perf: finalize k6 script, run on Dedicated window, generate result CSV + dashboard (owner)
- samir_eng: provision pool, seed cache, confirm quant builds (owner)
- maya_security: prepare SOC2 summary and draft note on Private timeline (owner)
- aj_patton: prepare pricing slide with both Hosted vs Dedicated POC numbers (owner)

olivia_sales: Can we get preliminary numbers within 48h after the run? Need to share with Nebula execs.

leo_perf: Yes — I'll post a short writeup in this thread with tables: RPS, p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per request for each variant.

aj_patton: Heads-up: Nebula also asked if we have any known p99 patterns under sequence >1024. If we see long tails we'll propose a graceful fallback policy (route to smaller quant model).

leo_perf: Good call. I'll include a small experiment: run a 30m session with 1200 tokens avg to capture tail behaviour.

olivia_sales: Thanks team. I'll loop in the Nebula technical contact post-provisioning. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Run window confirmed and creds posted to ephemeral channel #poc-nebula-health (expires in 14d).
